nodes.label: Synthetic Loopback Benchmark Scope
nodes.observations: Apple M1 Pro, native loopback execution, one I/O thread, 10000 keys per set, three four-second rounds per scenario. Synthetic data on a shared machine with preloaded cache and no misses; excludes TLS, S3 and recovery. RAM sampled 0.5 seconds after preparation does not establish stable or peak usage. Error bars show round minima and maxima, not confidence intervals.

nodes.label: CrabPack ligado e desligado
nodes.summary: O cenário ligado tinha 100% das chaves comprimidas antes da medição. O custo de CPU e latência depende do objeto e da concorrência.

nodes.label: Latência de GET individual
nodes.summary: Com CrabPack ligado, a média de GET individual aumenta nos quatro conjuntos: sessão 24,87→25,45 µs; produto 24,95→26,44 µs; API 22,07→25,00 µs; API com 40 itens 24,86→27,93 µs. O p99 permanece 63 µs para sessão e aumenta nos demais conjuntos.

nodes.label: GET sob carga concorrente
nodes.summary: Sob 48 conexões e pipeline 16, CrabPack ligado aumenta a latência em todos os conjuntos: sessão 0,524→0,806 ms; produto 0,497→0,796 ms; API 0,519→0,798 ms; API com 40 itens 1,591→2,866 ms.

nodes.label: RAM por chave após treino
nodes.summary: A amostra com CrabPack ligado aumenta RAM por chave para sessão 400→1773 B, produto 370→1458 B e API 395→1773 B; reduz para API com 40 itens 4184→1982 B. A RAM foi amostrada 0,5 s após preparar o conjunto e não representa consumo estável ou pico.

nodes.label: Metodologia e limites do benchmark
nodes.summary: Apple M1 Pro, execução nativa e loopback, uma thread de I/O, 10.000 chaves por conjunto e três rodadas de quatro segundos por cenário. Dados sintéticos em máquina compartilhada, cache pré-carregado e zero misses. GET inclui rede local e resposta; CPU/GET mede o servidor. Traços mostram mínimo e máximo das três rodadas, sem intervalo de confiança. Não mede TLS, S3 ou restauração após falha. Análise datada de 11/10/2026.

nodes.label: CrabPack Read Latency

For the 3913-byte API JSON object, loaded GET rises from 1.591 to 2.866 ms and CPU/GET rises from 2.050 to 3.702 microseconds.

nodes.rationale: Smaller compressed representation does not guarantee lower total sampled RAM for small values; the observed memory benefit depends on the object.

nodes.rationale: The observed smaller stored data and larger physical RAM must be interpreted as distinct measurements; this diagnostic does not establish which overhead caused the difference.

nodes.label: Mandatory Redis differential tests
nodes.rationale: CRABCACHE_REQUIRE_REDIS=1 prevents a missing Redis executable from silently turning differential tests into a false positive; Linux and macOS execute 100 seeds in release mode.

nodes.label: Test gated multiarchitecture Docker publishing
nodes.rationale: Docker publishing depends on the Redis-backed test job and builds linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 images with both version and latest tags.

nodes.label: Validated background dictionary training
nodes.rationale: Prefix ends at the first colon within 32 bytes; background sampling keeps at most 1000 samples or 256 KB per prefix. Train on four fifths and validate on one fifth in a blocking thread; reject ratios below 1.25x and retry after ten minutes. At most 64 accepted dictionaries remain alive permanently for lock-free reads.

nodes.label: Byte exact Redis compatibility validation
nodes.rationale: Random valid and invalid commands compare Redis and CrabCache responses byte for byte; numeric TTL tolerance includes request duration, -1/-2 must match exactly, KEYS is sorted, and final values and TTLs are checked.

nodes.label: Sampled shard eviction and global evictor
nodes.norm_label: sampled shard eviction and global evictor
nodes.rationale: noeviction rejects writes above maxmemory; LRU, LFU and random policies first sample entries in the writer's shard, with a background evictor scanning shards when local removal is insufficient.

nodes.label: Lazy and min heap active expiration
nodes.norm_label: lazy and min heap active expiration
nodes.rationale: Lookups remove expired entries; a bounded background pass every 100 ms consumes per-shard deadline heaps, ignores stale heap entries and rebuilds heaps larger than twice the TTL key count.

nodes.label: Transparent decompression and write semantics
nodes.rationale: Codec::with_value decompresses into a thread buffer; content writes store plain values, while RENAME and expiry changes retain compression. used_memory and maxmemory account compressed size and INFO exposes per-shard compression totals.

nodes.label: 300000 key synthetic JSON CrabPack results
nodes.rationale: Require 100 percent compression before measurement and full byte-for-byte verification afterward. Median incremental footprint savings versus Redis 8.10.2 were 61.3 percent sessions, 63.4 percent products and 55.0 percent API; decompression reduced measured GET throughput.

nodes.label: Node Redis cache aside integration
nodes.rationale: A pinned node-redis 4.7.1 example reads cache first, fetches simulated origin data on misses and caches with EX 30; the origin remains authoritative and applications must handle invalidation and cache unavailability.

nodes.label: CrabPack runtime configuration
nodes.rationale: Compression defaults to disabled; enabled defaults are 60 seconds idle and minimum 64 bytes. CONFIG SET changes only the current process; disabling future compaction leaves packed values readable.

nodes.label: October 11 complementary CrabPack read analysis
nodes.rationale: Four synthetic JSON datasets with 10000 keys each, three four-second rounds, one I/O thread and shared-machine loopback; GET and CPU means are count-weighted and must not be merged with the separate 300000-key audit.

nodes.label: Adaptive connection distribution
nodes.rationale: Activate ceil(connections/io-conns-per-thread) threads, default threshold 32, assigning new connections to the least loaded active thread. Light load wastes CPU when spread over many idle threads; existing connections never migrate.

nodes.label: Single write response batching
nodes.rationale: Execute every complete command in the read buffer and accumulate responses for one write, flushing early beyond 64 KB, to amortize syscalls under pipelining.

nodes.label: Fixed blocks of 256 entries
nodes.rationale: Fixed 4 KB blocks never move as a Vec would during growth, avoiding spare capacity and copies while retaining constant-time positions for random eviction sampling; hash indexes store u32 positions.

nodes.label: Sixteen byte entry layout
nodes.rationale: A 16-byte entry points to one allocation containing key and value with optional TTL and compression metadata; absent optional fields cost no allocation bytes. Unsafe storage code is isolated in src/store/entry.rs.

nodes.label: CrabPack prefix dictionary compression
nodes.rationale: Small cache values compress poorly alone but values sharing a key prefix have common structure; train a shared zstd dictionary per prefix and compress each eligible idle value individually.

nodes.label: Incremental bounded RESP parser
nodes.rationale: Preserve partial multibulk state and already-scanned inline positions for linear parsing. Redis-compatible protocol limits and per-client buffer bounds constrain CPU and memory consumption; arguments borrow input bytes until a write stores values.

nodes.label: Immediate mimalloc page purging
nodes.rationale: purge_delay=0 returns free pages immediately; the default delay left idle threads retaining released index-growth memory, measured at about 14 bytes per key.

nodes.label: Compression outside shard locks
nodes.rationale: Copy eligible entries under lock, compress outside it, then replace only if the entry has not changed; require at least one eighth savings and respect idle time and minimum size.

nodes.label: CrabPack phase one lifecycle limits
nodes.rationale: Dictionaries are not retrained, frequently read packed keys remain compressed until rewritten, and initial physical memory may rise while freed blocks await whole-page reclamation.

nodes.label: Thread per core I/O runtimes
nodes.rationale: Each I/O thread owns a single-thread Tokio runtime and event driver; reading, execution and response remain on the same thread to avoid cross-thread wakeups. Earlier work stealing lost per-core efficiency.

nodes.label: Physical memory and performance measurement limits
nodes.norm_label: physical memory and performance measurement limits
nodes.rationale: Payload ratio is not process footprint; post-load samples are not peak bounds, macOS footprint differs from Linux RSS, one I/O thread does not impose CPU affinity, and three shared-machine repetitions do not establish significance or production scalability.

nodes.label: Bounded in flight pipeline accounting
nodes.rationale: At client shutdown the server may have executed up to connections times pipeline more GETs than client-counted replies; negative differences or differences above that bound invalidate the run.

nodes.label: Experimental strings only cache scope
nodes.rationale: Version 0.3 is educational and experimental, supports strings only, and has no persistence, replication, transactions, Lua, pub/sub, or Redis collection types.
